w: At 10.00 am, Swamishri blessed the special kishore assembly. Thereafter Swamishri presided over a meeting on BAPS earthquake rehabilitation project.
In the late afternoon, from 5.00 pm to 7.15 pm, Swamishri resumed the earthquake rehabilitation meeting.

During the evening Satsang assembly Swamishri discoursed on the fleeting nature of the world (Sankhya), "If one realizes that everything will perish then one will be redeemed of ego and jealousy. Whatever tendencies of greed we have is because of lack of 'Sankhya Vichar'. After dinner, Swamishri resumed with the earthquake rehabilitation meeting.

An Idol of Service During a special kishore assembly, Swamishri was watching a skit that highlighted the importance of service. The skit was about a kishore assembly. The scene was the kishore assembly. The seating arrangement for Thakorji, sadhus and kishores were disorganized. The principal kishore coordinator arrives and then waits to observe what happens. As the kishores start arriving they all pass comments but do not tidy the situation. Finally the coordinator scolds them and he too leaves without properly arranging the situation. Thereafter a question answer session followed with Swamishri. When Swamishri took leave of the assembly, instead of going towards the exit door, he went to the skit scene. Swamishri went to the disorganized seat of Thakorji and said, "Let me do 'seva' before leaving. When no one did it then let me do it. Maharaj will be pleased." Swamishri bent low and organized the green cloth placed for Thakorji's seat (asan) and then happily took leave of the assembly. The entire assembly of kishores were amazed that even at 80 years of age Swamishri naturally grasped upon the opportunity of doing service.
Just as we look after land and property, similarly we should look after God because He is valuable.
It is more important to consolidate one's own satsang rather than consolidating another's because if one's own satsang is strong then others will be inspired by it.
One should not see and enjoy that which affects one's morality.
If one conquers a king one gains his whole kingdom. Similarly if one conquers ego, which is the king of all desires, one conquers all desires.

A devotee youth explained to Swamishri the details of a business he wished to do. Then he asked, "A devotee has asked me to form a partnership with him, but when I talked to him about making it official on a written document he said, 'Where is the need for us to have it documented? Between you and me we have Swamishri, so why worry?'

Swamishri replied with a word of advice, "As devotees, you are both fine. I bless both of you. However, your partnership must be signed and documented. Then, later, you won't have any problems. You must be clear as to what percentage is yours and his in the business. Do not be unclear in such matters. You must have it on a written document as prescribed in the Shikshapatri."

The owner and editor, Kishorebhai Kamdar and Milanbhai respectively, of a weekly magazine for Indians, 'Gujarat Sandesh', came to seek Swamishri's blessings. Swamishri sanctified their magazine before Thakorji and advised, "Alongwith other news include religious news, too. The new generation needs to know of it. Give that which has a good (positive) effect on the lives of Hindu boys. Since you have 'Sandesh' (means News or Message) as part of the magazine's name you also need to give God's message. Do not take advertisements that promote violence. Take such news that inspire values in people."

Swamishri's message is a guiding principle for all news media. As one who is active in solving the social ills that prevail in our society, Swamishri perfectly guides and advises on all matters of society.

When Swamishri arrived in the evening assembly Viveksagar Swami was explaining the unique attributes of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Thereafter the microphone used by Swamishri was arranged for his blessings, but it failed to function. The devotees in the assembly started chanting the holy name of Swaminarayan. A youth, Kishan Makwana, came and arranged another microphone for Swamishri.
"What have you done?" Swamishri amusingly referred to the situation.
"I haven't done anything. Your mic has broken down," the youth replied.
Swamishri replied, "My mic never breaks down. Maharaj, Swami, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogi Bapa speaks through it."
Swamishri naturally revealed that God and his gurus speak through him.

When Pramukh Swami Maharaj came for darshan around the mandir, Vishal Brahmbhatt, a mandir volunteer standing in front of the room of Bhagatji Maharaj, spoke a saying of Swami: "Keep the one resolve that we want to go to Akshardham." Then he said to Swamishri, "You will take me to Akshardham, won't you?"

Swamishri said joyfully, "Where is the question of taking you? The moment you resolve, you have already set off..." In a single sentence Swamishri revealed the power of having attained the manifest form of God.

ds.t: "You will take us to Akshardham, won't you?"
w: When Pramukh Swami Maharaj came for darshan on the parikrama (circumambulation path) of the mandir, Vishal Brahmbhatt, a mandir volunteer standing near Bhagatji Maharaj's room, recited a saying of Swami: "Keep just one resolve: 'I want to go to Akshardham.'" Then he said to Swamishri, "You will take us to Akshardham, won't you?"

In a joyful mood Swamishri said, "Where is the question of taking you? No sooner have you resolved it than you have set off..." In this one sentence Swamishri revealed the glory of having attained the manifest form of God.

When Pramukh Swami Maharaj came for darshan in the circumambulation path of the mandir, Vishal Brahmbhatt, a mandir volunteer standing near Bhagatji Maharaj's shrine, recited a saying of Swami: "Keep the one resolve, 'I want to go to Akshardham.'" Then he said to Swamishri, "Will you take me to Akshardham?"

Swamishri said joyfully, "Why speak of taking you there? We have not even made the resolve, and we have not set off..." In this one sentence Swamishri revealed the glory of having attained the manifest form of God.

During Swamishri’s morning puja, the stage was embellished with five kalashes that would crown the shikhars of Akshardham in New Delhi. During Swamishri’s puja, Dr. Swami, Ishwarcharan Swami, Viveksagar Swami and other sadhus performed the mahapuja rituals for the kalashes. Thereafter Swamishri placed Shri Harikrishna Maharaj on and worshipped the main kalash, standing at 8’4” with a circumference of 6’. Swamishri performed pujan, showered flower petals and rice grains and finally performed arti of all the kalashes. Swamishri also performed the pujan rituals of the giant 23’9” long flagpost weighing 450 kg. Swamishri was extremely pleased by the quality of the kalashes and blessed the sadhus and devotees involved in making them.
Dharmaprakash Swami had composed some couplets. He sang them while Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having breakfast.
About Akshardham he only said, "It is the pride of India..."
Then Swamishri immediately stopped him and said, "Not only of India; say it is the pride of the world."
The vision of Akshardham that was in Swamishri's heart was naturally revealed. Everyone corrected it and sang, "It is the pride of the world."
Dharmaprakash Swami had composed some couplets. He sang them while Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having breakfast.
About Akshardham he sang only, "It is the pride of India..."
Stopping him at once, Swamishri said in Hindi, "Not only of India. Say it is the pride of the world."
The vision of Akshardham in Swamishri's heart was naturally revealed. Everyone corrected it and sang: "It is the pride of the world."
Dharmaprakash Swami had composed some couplets. He sang them while Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having breakfast.
Referring to Akshardham, he only said (in Hindi), "It is the pride of India..."
Then Swamishri immediately stopped him and said, "Not only of India, say that it is the pride of the world."
The vision of Akshardham that was in Swamishri's heart naturally revealed itself. Everyone corrected the words and sang, "It is the pride of the world."
Dharmaprakash Swami had composed some couplets. He sang them while Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having breakfast.
Referring to Akshardham, he sang only, "It is the pride of India..."
Then Swamishri immediately stopped him and said, "Not only of India. Say it is the pride of the world."
The vision of Akshardham that was in Swamishri's heart naturally unfolded. Everyone corrected it and sang, "It is the pride of the world."
Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of arti and pujan of murtis for a hari mandir in Salavada in Panchmahal district.

A spiritual seeker came to Pramukh Swami Maharaj. After two or four deaths one after another in the family, he had become depressed and had taken to drinking. When this was told to Swamishri, Swamishri immediately said, "Do not drink at all. Each person stays here according to his lifespan and then goes. No one comes back by drinking. So keep the strength of God. Take refuge in God. Shriji Maharaj will be compassionate, so give up the addiction."
Then the seeker said, "Bapa! Will you come to take me at the end of my life?"
Swamishri said, "You do seva and devotion, so God will certainly come to take you."

A seeker came to Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Because of two or four deaths in the family one after another, he had become despondent and had taken to drinking. When this was told to Swamishri, Swamishri immediately said, "Do not take to addiction at all. Everyone stays here according to their lifespan and then goes. No one comes back through addiction. So keep the strength of Bhagwan. Take the refuge of Bhagwan. Shriji Maharaj will have mercy, so give up the addiction."
Then the seeker said, "Bapa! Will you come to take me at the end?"
Swamishri said, "You do seva and you do devotion, so Bhagwan will certainly come to take you."
During Mahant Swami Maharaj's breakfast, Amrutcharitdas Swami recalled an old memory and said to Swamishri:

"In 2002 you were visiting homes in Parsippany (US). The visits ran over and you lost your afternoon rest. At night we apologised: 'You had to bear hardship, your schedule was not kept; please forgive us.'
An ordinary person would certainly get angry, but you said, 'My experience for 40 years is that it is always like this.'
Then I asked, 'When this happens, what thought do you have?'
You said, 'I do not even make a resolve about what is going to happen one second later.'"
Who else in the world could say such a sentence?

Mahant Swami Maharaj came by plane from Kolkata to Ahmedabad. From the airport he went by car straight to the "BAPS Yogiji Maharaj Hospital" for necessary tests. After the tests were completed, he went to rest. On waking, concerned about others, Swamishri asked, "Are any sadhus admitted here?"
His attendant, Munichintandas Swami, said, "There is one, Harinarayandas Swami."
"Come, let us go and meet him," said Swamishri.
The attendant said, "Please sit. He will come for your blessings."
After a while Harinarayandas Swami came. As he was receiving Swamishri's blessings, Munichintandas Swami asked Swamishri, "How many times have you brought him back (from Akshardham)?"
"Three times," said Swamishri.
Harinarayandas Swami said, "Since you gave your blessings, there has been no pain at all."
Trying to steer the conversation towards his own powerlessness, Swamishri said, "In Devgadh Baria my finger got caught in a folding chair; it hurt for three days..."

By showing his own powerlessness, Swamishri tried to hide his divine power, but everyone was a witness to this incident: it was by Swamishri's own divine power that Harinarayandas Swami had received new life.

ds.t: Because it is the first time
w: Coming to the mandir, Mahant Swami Maharaj first went to the Abhishek Mandapam. After darshan, abhishek and circumambulation, he expressed a wish to do dandvat. Keeping Swamishri's weakness in mind, the senior sadhus requested Swamishri not to do dandvat.
Swamishri said, "It is the first time, so..."
Giving in, the sadhus said, "But it would be better if you did them upstairs..." Swamishri accepted the request.
Swamishri never misses a single chance to offer devotion, even creating a reason to do so.

ds.t: I ask my stomach, not my tongue
w: When Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for his meal, Viveksagardas Swami poured out a stream of talk to awaken Swamishri's interest in eating and to inspire him. Recalling Yogi Bapa, he said, "Yogi Bapa used to say, 'I like dry vegetable curry very much, and among meals I like puranpoli very much...' So what do you like?"
Swamishri laughed and said, "I have never thought about it."
Oh! What a height of freedom from attachment to taste!!
Viveksagardas Swami exclaimed, "There is no need to think about it... one just knows, doesn't one?"
Swamishri said, "I eat by asking my stomach, not my tongue."
